property_summary: After a call to Put, the total balance of the caller in the Acc mapping cannot exceed the sum of all msg.value sent to the contract by that caller, but the buggy version allows an overflow to reset the balance to a smaller value.

After any sequence of calls to Put by any address, the balance recorded in Acc for that address must equal the sum of all msg.value sent by that address through Put and the fallback, but the mutant allows overflow to wrap the recorded balance arbitrarily, breaking this invariant.

After a call to Put, if msg.value is not zero, the caller's balance in the Acc mapping must strictly increase by exactly msg.value, but the buggy version can cause the balance to increase by a smaller amount due to overflow wrapping, violating the equality.

For any caller, after any sequence of Put calls, the contract's ETH balance must be at least the sum of all caller balances in the Acc mapping; the mutant can overflow a caller's balance so that it wraps to a small value, making the sum of recorded balances smaller than the contract's actual ETH, violating the invariant.
After any call to Put, the caller's recorded balance must be at least the msg.value sent in that call, but the mutant allows overflow to make the new balance smaller than msg.value.
For any call to Put, the increase in the caller's balance recorded in Acc must equal the msg.value sent; the mutant adds only half, violating this equality.

After calling Put, the sum of all Acc balances plus address(c).balance must equal the total msg.value sent across all calls; the mutant adds only half, so it captures less than the full sent value, violating the global balance invariant.

For any actor, after a Put call with positive value, the change in the contract's total Acc balance across all addresses must equal the total msg.value received; the mutant adds only half, so its Acc total increases by less than the ether received.

For any call to Put with a given value, the contract's Ether balance must increase by the full msg.value; the mutant adds only half to Acc but the contract still receives the full Ether, so address(c).balance increases by the full amount while the sum of Acc balances increases by only half, making the difference detectable via total Acc balance vs. contract balance.

For any call to Put by any sender, the increase in the contract's Ether balance must not exceed the increase in the sender's recorded Acc balance by more than the Acc balance increase itself; the mutant adds only half, so the contract balance increases by the full msg.value while Acc balance increases by half, making the contract balance change more than double the Acc balance change.
Put MUST allow the caller to set a future unlockTime when the argument is greater than block.timestamp; the bug ignores the argument and sets unlockTime to block.timestamp.

After Put is called with a future timestamp argument, the reference contract's Acc[caller].unlockTime equals that future timestamp; the buggy contract's unlockTime equals the current block.timestamp, which will be strictly less.

After a call to Put with an unlockTime greater than block.timestamp, the unlockTime stored for the caller in the reference is strictly greater than block.timestamp, whereas in the mutant it equals block.timestamp; this difference is observable via the public Acc getter.

After a call to Put() with an unlockTime greater than block.timestamp, a subsequent call to Collect() that is attempted after the argument unlockTime but before it in the mutant should succeed only in the reference contract and fail in the mutant contract.

After Put with an unlockTime > block.timestamp, the reference stores that future time, so a Collect call after block.timestamp but before the future time reverts; the bug stores block.timestamp, so the same Collect call succeeds, violating the expected revert behavior.
After Put is called, the unlockTime stored in the contract must be at least block.timestamp for the reference contract; the buggy version can set unlockTime to a value less than block.timestamp.

After Put, the unlockTime stored for the caller must be at least block.timestamp for the reference; the bug sets unlockTime to _unlockTime, so when _unlockTime < block.timestamp, unlockTime < block.timestamp.

After a Put call with _unlockTime less than block.timestamp, the reference contract stores unlockTime >= block.timestamp, while the buggy contract stores unlockTime == _unlockTime < block.timestamp, allowing immediate Collect before the intended lock period.
After Put, unlockTime for the caller must be at least block.timestamp; the bug sets it to _unlockTime, violating this when _unlockTime < block.timestamp.

After calling Put with any _unlockTime, a subsequent attempt to Collect any amount before the recorded unlockTime must always revert for the reference contract; the bug allows _unlockTime < block.timestamp, making unlockTime in the past so Collect succeeds immediately before the intended lock period.
After any call to Put, the sender's Acc balance must equal the sum of the previous balance and the msg.value sent, but the mutant fails to add msg.value so the balance remains unchanged.
After any call to Put(uint) with a positive msg.value, the sender's Acc balance must increase by exactly the msg.value sent, but the mutant fails to add msg.value so the balance remains unchanged.
After Put, the sender's Acc balance must be strictly greater than the previous balance when msg.value > 0; the mutant leaves it unchanged because the balance increment is deleted.

After a successful call to Put with any msg.value, the contract's ether balance must increase by exactly msg.value; the mutant fails because it never forwards the received ether or stores it, so the contract balance stays the same.

After any call to Put with a msg.value, the sum of all Acc balances across all addresses ever deposited must equal the contract's ether balance; the mutant omits the balance increment so contract balance permanently diverges from the tracked user balances.
After any payable Put call, acc.unlockTime must equal the max of the given _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant fails to update it.

After two consecutive calls to `Put` with distinct `_unlockTime` values where the second `_unlockTime` is later than the first and both are in the future, the reference contract's unlock time equals the second (later) value while the mutant retains the first (earlier) value, so a `Collect` that succeeds on the mutant before the later time will fail on the reference.

After a Put call, the contract's Acc[caller].unlockTime equals the max of the provided _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the mutant fails to update unlockTime so it retains the previous value instead of the new max.

After three consecutive Put calls by the same caller, where the second call sets a high future unlock time and the third call sets a low past unlock time, the reference contract's unlock time equals the high future time from the second call, while the mutant's unlock time becomes the previous value (from the first call or default), making Collect succeed earlier on the mutant.

For any caller, after a successful Put where the provided _unlockTime is greater than block.timestamp, the caller's unlockTime must be updated to that provided _unlockTime; the mutant does not update it, so the unlockTime remains the previous value.

For any address calling Put, the resulting balance in acc must equal the previous balance plus msg.value (i.e., no overflow can occur), and the bug violates this by allowing silent overflow when a large balance is added.

For any actor sending any amount via Put, the contract's Acc balance for that actor after the call must be strictly greater than or equal to the balance before the call (i.e., no silent overflow reduction), and the buggy version violates this when an overflow wraps the balance to a smaller value.

After any Put call the resulting holder balance is exactly the sum of the previous balance and msg.value (the operation never wraps/saturates differently), which the buggy overflow violates by wrapping to a smaller value.

For any actor and any amount msg.value, if a Put call succeeds without reverting, then the contract's Acc balance for that actor must be at least the sent value (ensuring no silent overflow to a value less than msg.value), which the buggy version violates by allowing overflow that wraps the balance below msg.value.

After a successful Put call, the resulting Acc balance for the sender must be at least msg.value (i.e., no silent overflow that wraps the balance below the sent value), which the buggy version violates when the pre-existing balance plus msg.value overflows.
A Collect call that transfers funds before the unlock time must revert.
A Collect must revert if the block timestamp is not past the unlock time.
Collect must not revert when called after Put with a future unlock time and a balance increase.
